extraFacts.fact: ASME B16.9 covers factory-made wrought butt-welding fittings (elbows, tees, crosses, reducers and caps): overall dimensions, tolerances, ratings, testing and marking. In it, the centre-to-end dimension of a long-radius elbow is 1.5 times the nominal pipe size and that of a short-radius elbow is 1 times the nominal pipe size.
extraFacts.source: ASME B16.9 scope and elbow dimension tables

extraFacts.fact: ASTM A403/A403M covers wrought austenitic stainless steel piping fittings, including grades WP304 and WP316, and ASTM A960 gives the common requirements for wrought steel piping fittings.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A403/A403M and ASTM A960 scope

extraFacts.fact: MSS SP-43 covers wrought and fabricated butt-welding fittings for low-pressure, corrosion-resistant applications, in the lighter Sch 5S and Sch 10S wall thicknesses.

For gas tungsten arc welding of stainless steel, ER308L filler is used for 304 and ER316L filler for 316, and the weld should be cleaned, pickled and passivated after welding to restore corrosion resistance.
extraFacts.source: AWS A5.9 filler metal classification and general stainless welding practice

extraFacts.fact: 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 austenitic stainless steel (carbon 0.03 % maximum), which is why it can be welded without carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries; it contains molybdenum for resistance to chloride pitting.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A240 / A276 chemical composition limits for UNS S31603
